PullRequest.Title: sessions: separate Work and Personal contexts in the Agents window
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Adds **Work** and **Personal** contexts to the Agents window sidebar, so work sessions and personal ones (side projects, quick questions) are listed separately.

This is not a harness switch. Both contexts use the same agents, account, tools, settings, and permissions. They organize the sessions list.

### What switching between Work and Personal does

- **Changes:** which sessions, pins, groups, comparisons, archived sessions, drafts, and schedules are listed, and which folder New Session starts in.
- **Does not change:** your account, agents, tools, or permissions. It doesn't close the open conversation or discard unsent input either. The switch tooltips and the accessibility help say this.

### What each context holds

- **Folders belong to one context.** All sessions of a folder are listed together. A folder takes the context of the first session sent in it, or of the sessions already working there. Folders with sessions from before this change stay in Work.
- **Sessions without a folder** (quick chats) belong to the tab they were started in, and are listed in each context's Chats section.
- **Moving:** *Move Folder to Personal / Work* in the context menu of a session or a folder header moves the folder and all its sessions. *Move to Personal / Work* moves a session that has no folder.
- **New Session** starts in the folder of the session being shown, if it is in the selected context. Otherwise it starts in that context's most recently used folder. In Personal with no personal folder yet, it starts without a workspace.
- **Sending in a folder of the other context** (in the foreground) switches the tab to that context, so the new session stays in view.
- **Grouping** is the same in both contexts, so the usual grouping options work in each.

### UI

- The switch uses `$(briefcase)` Work and `$(home)` Personal, so the two are easy to tell apart from coding or chat icons.
- Uses the accessible segmented radio control and supports Left/Right Arrow.
- Other hosts of the shared Sessions view keep their mixed list.

### Possible next steps (not in this PR)

What could differ between the contexts beyond the list: the account, MCP servers and tools, instructions and memory, and the default agent, model, and approvals for each context.

## How to test

1. In Work, start a session in a folder. Switch to Personal: it is not listed. Switch back: it is listed under its folder.
2. In Personal, click New. With no personal folder yet, the composer starts without a workspace. Pick a new folder and send: the folder now belongs to Personal, and New in Personal starts there next time.
3. Right-click a Work session or folder header and choose *Move Folder to Personal*. The folder and all its sessions move to Personal.
4. In Personal, start a session in a folder that belongs to Work and send it. The tab switches to Work and the session is listed there.
5. Check that pinned, archived, grouped, saved-draft, scheduled, and comparison entries don't show up in the other context.
6. Reload. The selected tab, folder contexts, and session contexts persist.
7. Hover the switch and read the accessibility help (Alt+F1). Both say the contexts share account, agents, and tools.

## Validation

```sh
pnpm run typecheck-client
pnpm run valid-layers-check
git diff --name-only -- '*.ts' | xargs pnpm run oxlint
pnpm run build-fast --client-only
./scripts/test.sh --isolate --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/pendingSessionsList.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsViewPane.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newSessionAction.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionComparisonService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/scheduledChatsService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsArchiveActions.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionDraftsService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.test.ts
```

All 10 files pass (2 tests remain pending, as before). New tests cover:
- a folder's context overriding its sessions' own
- legacy `chat` values read as Personal
- New Session picking the selected context's most recent folder
- Personal falling back to an ordinary session when no workspace-less agent is available

Not run: the Code OSS window after the folder-based changes, integration suites, and screen-reader audio. The tab switch on send to a folder of the other context and the new context menu actions have no dedicated unit tests.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Traced the multi-selection delete action to deleteSessions, the agent-host provider's single batched removal event, storage's synchronous change emission, observableSignal's separate transaction per trigger, and the refreshSessions autorun. Only the duration and prevalence of large histories are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Renderer-thread session/chat iteration, filtered chat arrays, and observable dependency bookkeeping.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For D deleted sessions with stored category keys and R remaining listed sessions containing C chats in total, the added cleanup performs O(D * (R + C)) synchronous observer work, despite one provider-level removal event and coalesced rendering. Deleting legacy sessions without category keys does not trigger this work.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Additional synchronous renderer CPU work and temporary chat-filter allocations cause bulk-delete latency and UI stalls.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The agent-host provider published one batched removal event, causing one list refresh; the post-provider per-session cleanup did not mutate category storage or invalidate the all-sessions observer.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each successfully deleted session with a recorded category now synchronously invalidates the list's all-sessions/chat observer, including when none of the remaining sessions' categories changed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added removeCategory call at sessionsManagementService.ts:1826 executes inside the per-session loop after provider.deleteSessions. The new SessionCategoriesService storage listener (sessionCategory.ts:65-68) triggers a shared observableSignal for every removed category key, and the added getCategory read at sessionsList.ts:6074 subscribes the collection-wide refreshSessions autorun to that signal.
Findings.Title: Coalesce category invalidation during bulk deletion
Findings.Impact: Bulk-deleting hundreds of categorized sessions while hundreds remain adds hundreds of full remaining-session/chat scans on the renderer thread after backend deletion, delaying completion and making the Agents window unresponsive.
Findings.Evidence: views/sessionsListActions.ts:1766-1790 sends the selected collection to management.deleteSessions. baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts:8499-8530 deletes the targets and emits one removal event; the list refreshes once for that event. Management then invokes removeCategory separately for each deleted session. Storage.delete emits synchronously for each existing key (base/parts/storage/common/storage.ts), and SessionCategoriesService calls changed.trigger(undefined), which completes its own observable transaction synchronously. Each notification reruns sessionsList.ts:6067-6087 over every remaining session, filtering its chats and rebuilding observable dependencies before merely scheduling the rendered update for the next animation frame. That frame scheduling does not coalesce the collection scans.
Findings.Recommendation: Add a bulk category-removal operation that updates the category records while suppressing intermediate category invalidations, then notifies observers once after the batch. Ensure the shared signal actually uses that batch rather than starting an independent transaction for each key.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore the Agents sidebar and switch between Work and Personal; retain the shared mixed view in other hosts.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sidebar construction reads the stored selection, installs the small radio control, and builds the list. Selecting a category synchronously rebuilds the list; it does not await backend session loading or create agents.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize profile storage and persist the selected category and category records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing profile-map initialization, shared with application storage for the default profile; subsequent reads are local. Writes are accumulated by Storage.flushDelayer rather than sent once per category lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same storage map was initialized and used for sidebar state. The diff adds selection/category data, not a new per-row storage boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing storage initialization precedes cached reads. Selection persistence is asynchronous and not awaited by sidebar rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N already-loaded, deduplicated sessions and their chats, plus pending entries and comparison groups. List presentation caps do not bound the initial filtering scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer thread. One direct update on selection, with existing animation-frame coalescing for scheduled list changes. Service registration remains delayed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Category reads use the existing storage service's in-memory map, including absent category keys defaulting to Work. There is no per-session filesystem or IPC read. Profile initialization loads the storage map once; warm switches reuse it. The new service and control are disposed through existing ownership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced toggle registration, selection observables, list update, storage cache, and IPC storage client.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timing measurements or representative session-history distribution. New filtering and the small control add ordinary feature work, without a separate high-confidence regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent finding for initial rendering or tab switching. Existing expensive boundaries are not multiplied per session.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move a folder or selected workspace-less sessions to the other category.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action updates category storage synchronously and returns. Category observers scan existing sessions before scheduling the visible list update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update storage key-target metadata when new category keys are first introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most F + Q effective new keys; repeated writes to the same folder/value are suppressed. New key creation serializes profile key-target metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The category-move action and its category records did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Metadata serialization and observable notification run synchronously; the storage flush itself is deferred.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Flush accumulated folder/session category changes to profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Batched storage updates per flush, not an IPC operation for each folder member.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There were no category-move records to persist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the action's awaited critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F distinct folders plus Q workspace-less selected sessions. Multiple selected sessions of the same folder do not cause repeated effective changes once the folder value is stored.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous action loop and observer execution on the renderer thread. Animation-frame scheduling coalesces rendering but not the observer scans preceding it.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Storage.set suppresses identical values, so moving a folder with many sessions produces one effective category change, not one per member. Category lookups remain in-memory. Each distinct changed key invalidates the shared category signal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the move action, category setters, storage equality guard, and shared signal subscribers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A single-folder move is one invalidation. The cost of moving many independent folder/session keys depends on selection size and remaining history.
Scenarios.Verdict: Ordinary single-folder moves do not have per-member fan-out. Multi-key observer amplification shares the reported missing-coalescing mechanism and is not reported separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Bulk-delete categorized sessions while other sessions remain visible.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action awaits provider deletion, then removes each deleted session's category before the bulk operation resolves. These synchronous removals repeatedly rerun the remaining-session/chat observer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose each selected backend session through connection.disposeSession.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: D existing disposal requests for this provider, serially awaited, followed by one batched removal event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same D disposal calls and one batched provider event occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deletion must complete before management performs its added category cleanup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove each category key from profile target metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: D existing category-key removals, each potentially serializing the current key-target map.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The post-provider loop did not remove category records or trigger category observers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous cleanup after backend deletion; subsequent shared-signal invalidation causes the reported repeated scans.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Deletes are accumulated into a pending set and sent per flush; not D immediate storage IPC calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deferred persistence is not the reason for the renderer stall.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: D successfully deleted sessions with stored category keys, R remaining sessions, and C chats belonging to the remaining sessions. Added observer work is O(D * (R + C)); absent legacy category keys produce no change notification.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Providers are processed serially by management. The agent-host provider awaits disposeSession serially for its D targets and publishes one removal event. Afterwards category removals and their full observer scans are synchronous and unbatched; final rendering is animation-frame coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All category reads are cached storage-map accesses. Removing an existing key emits synchronously. Removing an absent key is a no-op. Database flush batching does not batch observableSignal transactions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: complete path from multiselection action through provider batching, synchronous storage emission, separate signal transactions, and the collection-wide autorun was inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact stall duration is unmeasured and depends on remaining sessions/chats and selected count. The multiplicative synchronous mechanism is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity missing-coalescing finding at sessionsManagementService.ts:1826.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or retarget a new session and send its first request, foreground or background.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: New Session chooses the active category's source folder, creates a draft, and captures its category. First send assigns a folder category if missing, optionally switches the tab, then follows existing preparation/configuration/send paths. Background sending remains detached after the existing handoff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve draft configuration and eagerly create the backend session via connection.createSession.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing one logical backend draft creation per newly created draft, guarded against duplicate eager creation; unchanged fallback behavior on failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both folder sessions and quick chats already used the same eager draft creation machinery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Draft UI construction starts backend work asynchronously; first send waits for the existing preparation/configuration requirements.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire/load the chat and submit the request through the existing chat service and provider transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same logical send per request; category metadata is not converted into additional sends.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider configuration, chat loading, and sending paths were used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing foreground send awaits submission; background send remains background.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist category assignment and identity transfer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Constant category mutations per draft/identity transition and one initial record per assigned folder, aggregated by storage flushing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No category records were assigned or transferred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cache mutation/notifications are synchronous; persistence is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one history scan to choose the most recent matching session when the active session is unsuitable. First category assignment for a folder scans merged sessions once; subsequent sends in that folder find its stored category immediately. Each identity transition transfers at most one category.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Category work is synchronous. Existing eager backend creation and configuration may overlap. Send configuration and deferred request resolution use the existing Promise.all; the diff adds no new concurrent backend launches per logical session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Selected and session/folder categories are in-memory storage reads. Folder assignment acts as a persistent positive result. Missing folder category incurs the one-time history scan; there is no remote discovery per session. Backend eagerCreate already guards its task/subscription and waits for existing configuration prerequisites.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: creation action, management ownership transitions, folder lookup, provider draft creation, eager backend guard, and send paths were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: History scan duration and remote provider latency are unmeasured. One-time folder scans and bounded identity transfers do not establish another independent actionable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding beyond the shared multi-key invalidation issue. Backend call cardinality and scheduling are preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Save and restore drafts and schedule a first request in its originating category.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Draft target capture includes one category read. Existing saved-draft persistence is delayed 300 ms. Scheduling still awaits time selection, attachment capture, and automation acceptance; restoring still follows existing provider configuration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read attachment bytes or resolve a text-model reference to capture scheduled input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing attachment-dependent reads; warm model references can reuse loaded models. No extra attachment reads are introduced by category propagation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same attachment capture callbacks and file/model operations were used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Capture must finish before the automation is submitted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit one automation definition and await its authoritative result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical automation creation per schedule, with existing stable-ID retry behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same automation creation path was awaited.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Scheduling confirmation waits for acceptance, unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist saved draft/handoff records including the category scalar.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing save and handoff-write counts, with constant extra metadata per record; category observation can retrigger target capture but normal saved-draft persistence remains debounced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Drafts and handoffs were already serialized and persisted without the extra category field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing synchronous serialization followed by deferred storage flushing; no new transcript/attachment serialization solely from the scalar.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of saved drafts/schedules and referenced attachments. Category adds one scalar per stored target. Handoff reconciliation assigns a category once for a dispatched session before marking groupApplied.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Saved-draft persistence uses the existing RunOnceScheduler. Tool schedule requests are sequenced by operationId, not globally; independent IDs can proceed concurrently as before. Handoff reconciliation runs synchronously over loaded catalogs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Category reads are cached. Draft saves retain the existing eligibility guards and debounce. Stable automation creation IDs and existing retry reconciliation remain authoritative; adding category does not create an extra automation request.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: target capture, save debounce/guards, attachment callbacks, per-key sequencing, handoff reconciliation, and automation submission were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Attachment sizes, catalog sizes, and service latency vary. The diff does not establish additional expensive boundary fan-out here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent high-confidence performance finding for draft/category propagation or scheduling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Launch, list, judge, and synthesize session comparisons within a category.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Comparison launch captures the selected category and passes it through existing attempt creation. The list resolves stored comparison categories and filters member rows. Judge and synthesis retain their existing prerequisites.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and submit backend sessions for attempts and subsequent comparison stages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing two to ten attempt sends, plus configured judge/synthesis stages. The diff passes the category without adding stages or calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same attempt count, Promise.all scheduling, and judge/synthesis session creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Comparison launch awaits existing attempt results; later stages await their existing prerequisites.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize comparison metadata including its category.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing comparison-state writes with one extra scalar per comparison; category storage mutations are bounded per participant.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same comparison records were persisted without category metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No newly awaited external operation is introduced by the field.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two to ten attempts per comparison, bounded by SESSION_COMPARISON_MAX_ATTEMPTS; number of retained comparison groups controls listing work. Each attempt adds bounded category mutation work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Attempt creation uses the existing map plus Promise.all, with timeout(0) before each attempt; the category field does not increase the existing maximum of ten attempt launches. Existing judge/synthesis ordering is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Category and participant lookups use loaded storage/provider state. Existing participant/session lookup and comparison persistence remain authoritative. No new remote metadata lookup is required to resolve the category.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected attempt limit, launch loop, category propagation, listing helper, and existing stage creation sites.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No benchmark of comparison-heavy histories. Some listing helper work is rearranged, but no independently material new scaling mechanism was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding. Category mutation amplification uses the same shared-signal mechanism already reported, with bounded attempt count per launch.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across the complete 34-file inventory and every diff page, with targeted caller, observer, storage, provider, draft, automation, and comparison tracing. Submitted one high-confidence medium-severity regression: per-session category cleanup defeats provider-level bulk deletion batching by synchronously rescanning all remaining sessions/chats for every removed category. No concrete performance regression fix requiring blame provenance was identified. Static read-only review; no measured latency claims.
